title: Count the allowed plans

blocks.text: A port authority wants to know how many berth-repair plans its rules leave open, to judge whether checking them one by one is realistic. Each candidate is a `Project` with a cost ($k), a `must_do` flag, an optional `parent` and an optional `group` of alternatives.
Write two functions in `count.py`. A plan is a set of project ids, and it is **allowed** when it keeps every row of the selection model, with $`x_i = 1`$ for each id in the plan:

items: `allowed(plan, projects, budget)` returns whether one plan keeps all four kinds of row.
`count_allowed(projects, budget)` checks every one of the $`2^n`$ subsets of the project ids, from the empty set to the full set, and returns how many are allowed.

blocks.text: `itertools.combinations(ids, k)` gives every subset of size `k`. The tests use at most five projects, so checking every subset is fast. About fifteen lines.

cases.says: every subset that keeps the budget, the must-do and the alternative rows is counted once
funding nothing is a plan too, and it is allowed when no project is must-do
a plan that spends exactly the budget keeps the budget row
the parent row is one-way: a parent alone counts, a child alone does not
